reason: Backend entry point and pre-development checklist for the Core-owned memory provider work.
Keep provider-neutral Core code, OS-specific Shell work, and shared protocol ownership in the correct packages.
Preserve foreground latency, volatile turn-context injection, detached post-turn work, and truthful tool-loop behavior.
Canonical records, authority epochs, ledgers, checkpoints, replicas, and outbox state require explicit Core-only migrations and transactions.
Separate non-secret provider settings from the provider-neutral secret backend and preserve effective-value precedence.
Provider, migration, synchronization, degraded, and recovery failures need typed retryable and terminal outcomes.
Diagnostics must remain useful without logging memory content, credentials, prompts, or unsafe provider payloads.
Setup, secret, backup, cutover, and destructive authority operations remain operator-only and explicitly gated.
Define one bounded canonical Memory Tool Contract with fenced results and no duplicate advertised tool suites.
Keep Hindsight MCP optional and prevent transport-specific schemas or defaults from leaking into canonical agent tools.
Provider status and long-running operation progress need producer-backed restoration rather than snapshot-only pseudo channels.
Apply Core/shared size, ownership, index, comment, and deterministic-test requirements across the large implementation.
Frontend entry point for Home/settings/operations integration and disposable-client invariants.
Authority, migration, sync, and setup state stay Core-owned; frontend cache remains non-authoritative and secret-free.
Protocol subscriptions and long-running setup/sync effects belong in hooks rather than presentation components.
Build guided setup, diagnostics, confirmations, loading, error, and empty states from established components.
Integrate memory setup and operations into the existing operator Home window without changing window authority boundaries.
Use discriminated provider/authority/operation states and schema-validated cross-layer payloads.
Preserve frontend file caps, indexes, deterministic tests, and separation of stateful hooks from views.
Trace authority, revisions, checkpoints, secrets, and progress end to end across Hindsight, Core, shared schemas, Shell, and UI.
Pin Hindsight and runtime claims to the evaluated 0.9.0 source/OpenAPI and contract tests rather than prose assumptions.
Evolve existing memory/config/operator seams without duplicating storage, tool, or status frameworks.
Authoritative map of the shipped Taki memory, prompt, maintenance, secret, deployment, and operator seams.
Exact Hindsight 0.9.0 REST, authentication, model, deployment, health, lifecycle, and operations contracts.
Frozen native-versus-adapter ownership and required journal, revision, snapshot, prompt, tag, recovery, and upgrade extensions.
